parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, no documented facility bans, custody-placement rules, police sweeps or border friction reaching visitors — the exposures a visitor actually faces are absent from the record. National anti-discrimination law explicitly covers gender identity, and entity-level hate-crime enhancements exist, though no prosecutions are documented (paper protections, weight limited). Against this: documented organised violence at LGBT public assemblies (2008 storming, 2014 attack despite police coordination, 2023 cancellation and chase), overwhelmingly hostile survey attitudes, and a local monitor's current (2024) finding of a worsening trend. Much of the hostility evidence is LGB-oriented, and dated; the violence episodes are event-centred, not a trans-specific campaign, and visitors are not documented targets. Thin-data context: I extrapolate from the decriminalised regime, paper protections, and documented societal hostility with unproven recourse — placing this below the acceptance-with-working-protections tier but above jurisdictions with any enforced trans-facing restriction. Friction and unreliably protective institutions, no universal exclusion: elevated-to-reduced boundary, ~0.57.
